questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which of these is a pulse?
questions.explanation: Moong, tur and gram are pulses. Wheat, rice and maize are cereals.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Butter, curd and ghee are all made from
questions.explanation: These dairy products are made from milk.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Edible oil can be obtained from the seeds of the
questions.explanation: Mustard, groundnut and sunflower seeds give oil.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which of these foods is made from the seed of a plant?
questions.explanation: Rajma beans are seeds. Spinach and cabbage are leaves and radish is a root.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: In the chain grass, deer, tiger, which statement is true?
options: Grass is eaten by the tiger directly
The deer is a herbivore and the tiger is a carnivore
questions.explanation: Deer eat grass and tigers eat deer, so the deer is a herbivore and the tiger a carnivore.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Name three different parts of plants that we eat and give an example of each.
questions.answer: Roots such as radish, leaves such as spinach and fruits such as banana.
questions.explanation: Different plant parts are used as food.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Plants make their own food while animals cannot. Explain how animals get their food.
questions.answer: Animals depend on plants, or on other animals that eat plants, for food. They cannot make food themselves.
keyPoints: Animals eat plants or other animals
questions.explanation: All animals depend on plants directly or indirectly.

questions.q: Which of the following is a good source of protein?
questions.explanation: Pulses, milk, eggs and fish are rich in proteins.

questions.q: Calcium in the diet is needed mainly for
questions.explanation: Calcium keeps bones and teeth strong.

questions.q: Which of these is a function of water in our body?
options: To help digest food and remove wastes
questions.explanation: Water helps in digestion, carries nutrients and removes waste through urine and sweat.

questions.q: Beriberi is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Lack of vitamin B1 causes beriberi.

questions.q: Which meal is the most balanced?
options: Chapati, dal, vegetables and a glass of milk
questions.explanation: It contains carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, minerals, fats and roughage.

questions.q: Name the components of food and say which ones give us energy.
questions.answer: The components are carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water and roughage. Carbohydrates and fats give energy.
questions.explanation: Each component has its own function.

questions.q: Why does a person doing heavy physical work need more energy-giving food than someone who sits at a desk?
questions.answer: Heavy work uses more energy, so the body needs more carbohydrates and fats to supply it.
questions.explanation: Energy needs depend on activity.

questions.q: Which of these is used for spinning yarn by hand?
questions.explanation: A takli or charkha twists fibres into yarn.

questions.q: The hairy coat of a sheep that is cut to get wool is called
questions.explanation: The fleece of a sheep is removed by shearing.

questions.q: Yarn is
options: A long continuous thread made by spinning fibres
A fabric made on a loom
questions.explanation: Fibres are twisted to make yarn.

questions.q: Which of these is an animal fibre?
questions.explanation: Silk comes from silkworms. Cotton, jute and coir are plant fibres.

questions.q: After harvesting, jute stems are soaked in water for some days. Why?
options: The fibre separates from the stalk more easily
questions.explanation: Soaking loosens the stems so that fibres can be peeled off.

questions.q: Describe how yarn can be made by hand.
questions.answer: Fibres are drawn out from a bunch of cotton and twisted using the fingers, a takli or a charkha to form a long thread.
questions.explanation: Spinning is twisting fibres into yarn.

questions.q: Why are cotton clothes preferred in hot summer weather?
questions.answer: Cotton absorbs sweat easily and lets it evaporate, so the body feels cool.
questions.explanation: Fabric choice depends on weather.

questions.q: Which of these floats on water?
questions.explanation: Cork is lighter for its size than water, so it floats.

questions.q: Which of these is soft?
questions.explanation: A sponge can be pressed easily.

questions.q: Which statement about oil and water is correct?
options: Oil floats on water as a separate layer
questions.explanation: Oil is lighter than water and does not mix, so it floats on top.

questions.q: Which of these can you see through clearly?
questions.explanation: Clear glass is transparent.

questions.q: A door is made of wood, but a window pane is made of glass. Why?
options: The glass lets light pass through while the wood blocks view and gives privacy
questions.explanation: Transparent glass lets in light and wood is opaque.

questions.q: Why are cups often made of ceramic or steel and not paper for hot tea at home?
questions.answer: Ceramic and steel are strong, do not dissolve or soften in hot liquid, and can be used again and again.
questions.explanation: Materials are chosen for their properties.

questions.q: Group these into sink or float in water: iron nail, cork, stone, wooden block, plastic bottle cap.
questions.answer: Sink: iron nail and stone. Float: cork, wooden block and plastic cap.
questions.explanation: Floating depends on how heavy the object is for its size.

questions.q: Which tool is used for sieving?
questions.explanation: A sieve has holes through which smaller particles pass.

questions.q: In sedimentation the heavier particles
questions.explanation: Heavy particles settle down in a liquid.

questions.q: Alum is added to muddy water because it
questions.explanation: Alum makes tiny particles stick together so they settle quickly.

questions.q: Wet clothes dry fastest when they are hung
options: In the sun on a windy day
Under the shade with no breeze
questions.explanation: Heat and wind speed up evaporation.

questions.q: A mixture of sawdust and iron filings is given. Which is a simple way to separate them?
questions.explanation: A magnet pulls out the iron filings, leaving the sawdust.

questions.q: What is sedimentation and decantation? Where are they used?
questions.answer: Sedimentation is the settling of heavy particles at the bottom. Decantation is pouring out the clear liquid above. Used for muddy water.
questions.explanation: These steps often come before filtration.

questions.q: Can sugar be separated from a sugar solution by filtration? Explain.
questions.answer: No. Dissolved sugar passes through filter paper with the water. It can be recovered by evaporating the water.
questions.explanation: Filtration only removes undissolved solids.

questions.q: The change of liquid water into ice is called
questions.explanation: Cooling turns a liquid into a solid, which is freezing.

questions.q: Which of these changes is slow?
questions.explanation: Rusting takes days or weeks, but the others happen quickly.

questions.q: Which change is caused by heating and cannot be reversed?
questions.explanation: A fried egg cannot go back to raw egg.

questions.q: Which of the following is a periodic change?
options: The change of day and night
questions.explanation: Day and night repeat at regular times.

questions.q: Bread is toasted. Which statement is true?
options: The change is irreversible because the bread changes permanently
questions.explanation: Toasted bread cannot return to soft bread.

questions.q: Give two changes that are caused by heating and two caused by cooling.
questions.answer: Heating: melting of butter, boiling of water. Cooling: freezing of water, condensation of vapour.
questions.explanation: Changes of state are due to heating or cooling.

questions.q: Describe the changes that take place when raw rice is cooked, and say if they can be reversed.
questions.answer: The rice softens, absorbs water and changes taste and colour. These changes cannot be reversed, so cooking is irreversible.
questions.explanation: Cooking makes permanent changes in food.

questions.q: The tiny pores on the surface of leaves are called
questions.explanation: Stomata let in gases and let out water vapour.

questions.q: A medium-sized plant with many branches near the base is a
questions.explanation: Shrubs are bushy with a stem that branches near the ground.

questions.q: The pea plant and the pumpkin plant are called climbers and creepers because their stems are
questions.explanation: Their stems are weak, so they climb on supports or spread on the ground.

questions.q: Which of the following leaves has reticulate venation?
questions.explanation: A peepal leaf has a net-like pattern of veins.

questions.q: A gardener ties a pea plant to a stick. Why?
options: The stem is weak and needs support
questions.explanation: A climber cannot stand without a support.

questions.q: Name the parts of a leaf and give the function of veins.
questions.answer: A leaf has a lamina (blade), a petiole and veins. Veins carry water and food in the leaf.
questions.explanation: The leaf is the food-making organ.

questions.q: Give two reasons why the roots are essential to a plant.
questions.answer: Roots hold the plant firmly in the soil and absorb water and minerals from it.
questions.explanation: Roots support the plant and supply water.

questions.q: The soft, bendable part of the ear is made of
questions.explanation: Cartilage is flexible and gives shape to the outer ear.

questions.q: Muscles help us move by
questions.explanation: Muscles contract and relax, pulling bones.

questions.q: The joint at the hip allows the leg to move
questions.explanation: The hip is a ball and socket joint that gives movement in all directions.

questions.q: Which animal has a body with six legs and wings that help it walk and fly?
questions.explanation: A cockroach can walk, run and fly using legs and wings.

questions.q: When you bend your elbow, which muscle contracts?
questions.explanation: The biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes when the arm bends.

questions.q: What is the function of the ribs?
questions.answer: Ribs form the rib cage, which protects the heart and lungs and helps in breathing movements.
questions.explanation: The rib cage surrounds the chest organs.

questions.q: Why is a skeleton useful to the body?
questions.answer: The skeleton gives shape, protects soft organs such as the brain and heart, and lets us move with muscles.
questions.explanation: Bones and muscles work together.

questions.q: Which of these is a living thing?
questions.explanation: Grass grows, reproduces and responds to its surroundings.

questions.q: Which of these animals lives on land?
questions.explanation: A lion is a terrestrial animal.

questions.q: A plant whose leaves float on the surface of a pond is
questions.explanation: Water lilies have broad leaves that float.

questions.q: Thick fur and a layer of fat help animals to live in
questions.explanation: Thick fur and fat reduce loss of body heat.

questions.q: A toy robot can walk and move its arms. Why is it not a living thing?
options: It does not grow, reproduce, breathe or need food
It is made by people so it is not real
questions.explanation: Movement alone does not make something living; living things grow, respire and reproduce.

questions.q: Name two living and two non-living components of a pond habitat.
questions.answer: Living: fish and water plants. Non-living: water and soil or rocks.
questions.explanation: A habitat has biotic and abiotic parts.

questions.q: Why do camels have broad, padded feet?
questions.answer: The broad feet spread out the weight of the animal so that it does not sink into the sand when walking.
questions.explanation: It is an adaptation for desert life.

questions.q: The distance between two cities is best measured in
questions.explanation: Long distances are measured in kilometres.

questions.q: The small unit used for the thickness of a coin is the
questions.explanation: A millimetre is one-tenth of a centimetre.

questions.q: A length of 1.5 m is equal to
The motion of a pendulum in a clock is
questions.explanation: A pendulum moves to and fro about a point, which is oscillatory and periodic.

questions.q: A student reads a length by looking at the scale from an angle. What is likely to happen?
options: The reading may be wrong due to a slanted view
questions.explanation: The line of sight should be vertical to the mark to avoid error.

questions.q: Why do we need standard units of measurement?
questions.answer: Standard units give the same result for everyone, so measurements can be compared and understood by all.
questions.explanation: Non-standard units like hand-spans vary.

questions.q: Explain how you could measure the length of the boundary of a circular plate using a thread and a ruler.
questions.answer: Wind the thread once along the edge of the plate, mark the length, straighten the thread and measure it with a ruler.
questions.explanation: A thread can follow a curved path.

questions.q: The bouncing back of light from a surface is called
questions.explanation: A mirror reflects light that falls on it.

questions.q: A shadow is formed on a
questions.explanation: A screen such as a wall shows the dark area.

questions.q: The device that uses a small hole to form images is called a
questions.explanation: A pinhole camera forms an inverted image through a small hole.

questions.q: Which statement about light is true?
options: Light needs air to travel only
questions.explanation: Light travels in straight lines and does not bend around opaque objects.

questions.q: In a shadow play, the puppet is moved closer to the screen. The shadow becomes
questions.explanation: Moving the puppet nearer the screen and away from the lamp reduces the shadow size.

questions.q: List the conditions needed to form a shadow.
questions.answer: A source of light, an opaque object in the path of the light and a screen.
questions.explanation: The opaque object blocks the light.

questions.q: Write one difference between a shadow and an image in a mirror.
questions.answer: A shadow is a dark area showing only the outline of the object, while an image in a mirror is formed by reflected light and shows details and colours.
questions.explanation: A shadow forms by blocked light and an image by reflected light.

questions.q: Which of these is a source of electricity?
questions.explanation: A cell supplies electric current.

questions.q: The torch uses
questions.explanation: A torch contains cells that supply electricity to the bulb.

questions.q: A circuit is called a closed circuit when
questions.explanation: Current flows only in a complete path.

questions.q: The two terminals of a bulb are connected to
questions.explanation: The ends of the filament are connected to the two terminals of the bulb.

questions.q: An electric plug has metal pins but a plastic body. Why?
options: Pins carry current and plastic protects us from shocks
questions.explanation: Metal conducts the current and the plastic is an insulator.

questions.q: What is the function of a switch in an electric circuit?
questions.answer: A switch opens or closes the circuit, so it can stop or allow current to flow.
questions.explanation: A switch breaks the path of the current.

questions.q: Describe how to test whether a pencil lead, a rubber and an iron nail are conductors using a tester.
questions.answer: Connect each material in turn between the free ends of a circuit with a cell and bulb. If the bulb glows, the material conducts; if not, it is an insulator.
questions.explanation: The bulb works as an indicator.

questions.q: A magnet has
questions.explanation: Every magnet has a north and a south pole.

questions.q: Which of these is attracted by a magnet?
questions.explanation: Iron is magnetic.

questions.q: Iron filings sprinkled on paper over a bar magnet mostly collect near
questions.explanation: The poles attract the most filings.

questions.q: A magnet can be used to pick up
questions.explanation: Steel contains iron and is attracted.

questions.q: Which observation proves that an unknown metal bar is a magnet and not just a piece of iron?
options: It is attracted by a known magnet
It repels the north pole of a known magnet when one of its ends is brought near
It sticks to a steel table
questions.explanation: Only a magnet can repel; iron is always attracted by either pole, so attraction alone does not prove it.

questions.q: State two properties of a magnet.
questions.answer: A magnet attracts magnetic materials and has two poles. A freely suspended magnet settles in the north-south direction.
questions.explanation: These are basic properties of magnets.

questions.q: A compass needle is placed on a table far from any magnet. Why does it still settle in the north-south direction?
questions.answer: The Earth behaves like a large magnet, so the needle, which is a small magnet, lines up with it.
questions.explanation: A compass works because of the Earth's magnetism.
